message.content:
Below are two ways you can provision a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

---

## 1️⃣  `gcloud` CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1. Create a project‑specific zone (replace <PROJECT_ID> & <ZONE>)
gcloud config set project <PROJECT_ID>
gcloud config set compute/zone us-central1-a   # or your preferred zone

# 2. Enable the required APIs (if not already enabled)
gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com \
                      cloudbilling.googleapis.com \
                      iam.googleapis.com

# 3. Create a service account key (optional but handy for automation)
gcloud iam service-accounts keys create ~/sa-key.json \
    --iam-account=compute-admin@<PROJECT_ID>.iam.gserviceaccount.com

# 4. Create the VM
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-instance \
    --machine-type n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30GB RAM – adjust as needed
    --image-family ubuntu-2004-lts \        # Ubuntu 20.04 LTS
    --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size 100GB \                # size of boot disk
    --boot-disk-type pd-ssd \               # SSD boot disk
    --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \   # 1 RTX A6000
    --maintenance-policy TERMINATE \        # terminate on host maintenance
    --restart-on-failure \                 # auto‑reboot on failure
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # optional init script
    --tags http-server,https-server \       # allow HTTP/HTTPS traffic
    --scopes https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform   # full access
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration (`n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPU + 30 GB RAM). |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Selects the OS image (Ubuntu 20.04 LTS). |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | Size/type of the root disk. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds GPUs; here we add one RTX A6000. |
| `--maintenance-policy` | How to handle host maintenance events. |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑reboot if the instance crashes. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional shell script that runs at first boot. |
| `--tags` | Network tags for firewall rules. |
| `--scopes` | IAM scopes for the instance’s service account. |

> **Tip:** If you plan to use the instance programmatically, consider creating a dedicated service account with only the permissions you need (e.g., `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1`, `roles/storage.objectViewer`, etc.) instead of granting full `cloud-platform` scope.

---

## 2️⃣  REST API (JSON payload)

If you prefer to use the raw REST API (or integrate into Terraform, Pulumi, etc.), here’s a minimal JSON body you can POST to the Compute Engine API:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-instance",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "<SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL>",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update && apt-get install -y python3-pip"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

### How to POST

```bash
curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d @instance-create.json \
     "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

Replace `<PROJECT_ID>` and `<SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL>` with your actual values. The `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token` command fetches an OAuth token that authorizes the request.

---

## Quick Checklist

- [ ] **Project ID** – replace `<PROJECT_ID>` everywhere.
- [ ] **Zone** – choose a zone that supports RTX A6000 (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`, etc.).
- [ ] **GPU quota** – make sure you have a GPU quota for `nvidia-tesla-a6000`. Request more via the Cloud Console if needed.
- [ ] **Billing** – ensure billing is enabled for the project.
- [ ] **Firewall** – the `http-server` and `https-server` tags automatically open ports 80/443. Add custom rules if you need other ports.

Once created, you can SSH into the instance:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-instance
```

And verify the GPU:

```bash
sudo lshw -C display
nvidia-smi
```

That’s it! You now have a ready‑to‑use Compute Engine instance with an RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.
